The goal is to find new and better ways to prevent, diagnose or treat diseases of dogs and cats. MedVet’s Clinical Studies Center facilitates high-quality clinical studies to advance the veterinary profession in caring for our beloved pets. Current Clinical Studies We have successfully completed single center and multi-center clinical studies evaluating diagnostic tests, pharmaceuticals, biologics, surgical procedures, and medical devices for acute and chronic pain, congestive heart failure and other cardiac diseases, osteoarthritis and other orthopedic diseases, cancer, seizure disorders, endocrine diseases, ophthalmologic conditions, and chronic skin diseases. You can explore our current clinical studies below. Experimental EGFR/HER2 Tumor Vaccine This is a USDA regulated scientific study. Enrollment is limited to dogs with osteosarcoma, hemangiosarcoma and transitional cell carcinoma. The vaccine is currently provided at no charge to the pet owners. As this is not a fully funded study, all costs associated with hospital visits, diagnostics and vaccine administration are the responsibility of the pet owner. If the vaccine receives approval, it will no longer be provided at no cost. To ensure all patients meet the enrollment criteria of having an expected prognosis that is greater than three months, MedVet hospitals are currently limiting enrollment to patients who are receiving appropriate standard of care therapies which may include surgery, chemotherapy, and/or radiation therapy depending on the tumor type. Patients being screened for enrollment with the intent to use the vaccine as a single agent treatment will not be considered. Study Locations MedVet Salt Lake City is currently enrolling patients. MedVet Cincinnati and MedVet Cleveland enrollment is limited to established patients with all treatment and follow-up visits being held at the same hospital. MedVet Pittsburgh enrollment is limited to dogs that live in Pennsylvania with all follow up visits being held at MedVet Pittsburgh. MedVet Chicago is currently pausing enrollment until further notice. Study Enrollment Criteria Histologically (biopsy) confirmed diagnosis of osteosarcoma, hemangiosarcoma, or transitional cell carcinoma.
